investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T22:22:48–52Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every sibling check's probe flow, the quota rejection at the shared upstream dependency (POST /api/agents) caused all downstream evidence collection to be skipped entirely, leaving the expected-output contract with zero evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) is the first operation in the remote-agent-create probe; when it receives a 409, the probe exits before collecting any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. The same rejection propagates identically to the remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime sibling probes, confirming the failure is rooted in the shared agent-creation step rather than in any individual check's logic. This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real backend quota condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T22:22:48–52Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every sibling check's probe flow, the quota rejection at the shared upstream dependency (POST /api/agents) caused all downstream evidence collection to be skipped entirely, leaving the expected-output contract with zero evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) is the first operation in the remote-agent-create probe; when it receives a 409, the probe exits before collecting any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. The same rejection propagates identically to the remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime sibling probes, confirming the failure is rooted in the shared agent-creation step rather than in any individual check's logic. This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real backend quota condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed because the agent runtime endpoint returned a 404, causing a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error that terminated the SSE stream immediately after generation_start. As a result, the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame and no image URL was produced, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api agent runtime endpoint targeted by the /api/generate/image/stream SSE probe is unreachable or returning HTTP 404. The stream opened (generation_start received), but the agent session could not be established (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED), causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of progressing to generation_completed. This is an eval-infrastructure or backend-routing failure localized to the production-api runtime environment and the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted.
proof: failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent = false — both contract assertions violated.

failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message='agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2012 — the check completed in ~2 seconds, consistent with an immediate 404 rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation failure.
failed-check.message: top-level check message repeats the 404 / SESSION_OPEN_FAILED text, confirming the error propagated from the stream frame to the check result.

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent equals true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 271–272); neither was satisfied.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1431-1439: runner calls apiSse(args, '/api/generate/image/stream', ...) — the 404 is returned by this endpoint in the production-api environment.
source.check-config.image-generation-stream: runtimeEnvironment=production-api, required=false, statusImpact=informational — failure is informational for status purposes, not a required check.
possibleCauses: The agent runtime harness backing /api/generate/image/stream is not deployed or not reachable in the production-api environment, causing the endpoint to return 404 at session-open time (strongest evidence: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED code and 404 message in failed-check.evidence).

The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable used by the eval runner is misconfigured or pointing to a stale/wrong host for the production-api runtime, causing the 404 (the error message explicitly names these variables as candidates).

The /api/generate/image/stream route or the agent runtime version deployed to production-api is incompatible with the version expected by the eval harness (the error message states 'running an incompatible version').

An authentication or routing layer in production-api is returning 404 instead of 401/403 for this endpoint, masking a credential or permissions issue with the token used by the eval runner (less likely given the explicit SESSION_OPEN_FAILED code, but not ruled out).
